item.title: The Houthi Threat: Is Trump Underestimating One of Iran’s Key Remaining Cards?
item.description: The Houthis have entered the war in Iran. Whether they choose to block Bab al-Mandab or not could have significant consequences for the global economy.

item.title: Who Is Winning the Iran War?
item.description: The United States and Israel are devastating Iran's leadership and inflicting significant damage on Iran's already-weak military. Iran, however, is hitting back, and the biggest long-term costs to the United States are likely to be felt outside the Middle East.

item.title: Iran Conflict Heightens Cyber Threats to U.S. Energy Infrastructure
item.description: As the Iran conflict intensifies, U.S. energy infrastructure faces escalating cyber threats from nation-state actors. Scale, age, and regulatory fragmentation leave the sector uniquely exposed. A successful attack would cascade across the entire U.S. economy.

item.title: Iran, Fertilizer, and Food Security: Risks, Impacts, and Policy Responses
item.description: The war with Iran is threatening global agriculture markets and food prices, with some impacts emerging and more expected in the coming months. What can policymakers do to protect farmers and consumers—in the United States and around the world?

item.title: Where Is Congress?
item.description: In this week's column, Bill Reinsch argues that Congress has ceded authority to the presidency and proposes reforms to strengthen the legislative branch’s effectiveness.

item.title: States Weekly: April 1, 2026
item.description: This edition of States Weekly covers April 1, 2026.

item.title: We Are Going Back to the Moon to Stay
item.description: NASA's plan to establish a base on the Moon is part of a strategic competition with China. The United States needs to be in it for the long game.

item.title: Cracking the Code on the Lunar Economy
item.description: To build a sustainable lunar economy, the United States must move beyond government-led models and adopt a commercially driven approach, treating the Moon as a real estate project anchored by public-private partnerships and an international Lunar Development Authority.

item.title: Artemis and the Economics of a Permanent Moonbase
item.description: Apollo proved we could go. Artemis must prove we can stay. That will require not just new technology, but a new approach to cost, partnerships, and political durability.
